causes.text: In late October 2023, CVS Health announced that its pharmacies would exclusively stock GSK's newly launched RSV vaccine Arexvy, rather than offering Pfizer's rival shot. Analysts noted that CVS's decision, combined with a competitive price point, helped GSK capture roughly two-thirds of all RSV vaccinations in the U.S. during the vaccine's first month on the market.

source_info.title: Pfizer's RSV vaccine lags GSK's as head-to-head competition underway

effects.text: On 1 November 2023, GSK raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts for the second time that year after reporting stronger-than-expected sales of its RSV vaccine Arexvy. The company said it accounted for about two-thirds of RSV doses administered at U.S. pharmacies; GSK shares initially gained more than 3% before slipping 1.3% as traders locked in profits.

source_info.title: GSK raises profit outlook again after successful RSV vaccine launch

causal_reasoning_chain.description: CVS's decision to offer only GSK's Arexvy at its pharmacies dramatically increased the vaccine's visibility and convenience for consumers. By excluding Pfizer's Abrysvo from its shelves, CVS effectively channelled demand toward GSK's product during the crucial launch window.

Because CVS is one of America's largest pharmacy chains, its exclusive stocking policy translated into real-world market share gains. Analysts observed that GSK's shot captured about two-thirds of RSV vaccinations in 2023, giving the company pricing power and encouraging management to upgrade forecasts.

When GSK reported third-quarter results days later, the surge in Arexvy sales allowed it to raise full-year guidance for a second time. Investor enthusiasm initially pushed the share price up more than 3%, though profit-taking later pared the gain to a 1.3% drop by the close.

rationale: CVS's exclusive stocking of GSK's vaccine effectively shut out Pfizer from a significant portion of the U.S. pharmacy channel. This dominant distribution boosted early uptake and enabled GSK to beat expectations, providing the basis for a confident guidance upgrade.
counterfactual_analysis: If CVS had stocked both companies' vaccines equally, GSK's share of RSV vaccinations would likely have been lower. Without such a commanding market share, the company may have been more cautious in raising its annual forecast, resulting in a smaller or delayed stock reaction.

adversarial_confounders.text: Pfizer's vaccine Abrysvo faced limited initial supplies and insurance coverage hurdles during the same period.
adversarial_confounders.impact: These operational issues may have independently depressed Pfizer's uptake and boosted GSK's market share beyond the impact of CVS's decision.

details.commentary: CVS's choice to stock only Arexvy concentrated retail channel power in GSK's favor at the start of the RSV season. Exclusive access to a major chain limited Pfizer's ability to compete for pharmacy-administered doses, reinforcing GSK's early lead in the category.

High concentration among U.S. pharmacy chains and insurer formularies means channel decisions can quickly reshape vaccine uptake. Within that economic structure, CVS's exclusivity helped GSK translate strong clinical data into real-world share, supporting its upgraded guidance even if the share-price reaction was muted by profit-taking.

Exclusive placement boosted early vaccination volumes, which in turn improved inventory planning, physician awareness and payer confidence in Arexvy. Those reinforcing effects underpinned GSK's willingness to raise forecasts, even though short-term trading flows caused the stock to give back initial gains.
